farfield.options.title: Farfield Settings
farfield.options.rendering.tooltip: Draw the terrain beyond the render distance as levels of detail. Off shows only what the game draws.
farfield.options.detail.tooltip: Largest size of a distant voxel on screen before finer detail takes over. Lower is finer and costs more video memory and GPU time: 2 px uses about six times the memory of the default, 6 px.
farfield.options.textures.tooltip: Distance up to which distant terrain shows block textures; farther faces show their mean color. Textures cost almost nothing on the GPU. Default: all distances.
farfield.options.fog.tooltip: Where the fog becomes opaque over the distant terrain, in normal dimensions such as the Overworld. Nothing beyond it is drawn, so a closer fog also lightens the GPU. Off: no fog, the edge of the distant terrain shows.
farfield.options.thick_fog.tooltip: The same in dimensions with thick fog, such as the Nether. Vanilla: distant terrain fades into the game's own fog, so little of it shows.
farfield.options.noise_preview.tooltip: Show terrain the world has not generated yet, coarsely, from the world seed: relief, water and a surface color, without trees or buildings. Real terrain replaces it as you explore. Single player only.
farfield.options.mesh_threads.tooltip: Threads that turn stored terrain into distant terrain to draw. More threads show new terrain sooner after a teleport and take more processor time. Auto: one per four logical processors, 1 to 4.
farfield.options.preview_threads.tooltip: Threads that compute the preview of terrain not generated yet. More threads finish the preview sooner and take more processor time. Auto: one per four logical processors, 1 to 4. Single player only.
farfield.options.level_colors.tooltip: Tint distant terrain by level of detail: red 1 block, orange 2, yellow 4, green 8, blue 16 blocks per voxel.
